shares_note: Post-Covelya-close fully diluted estimate: ~306.5M current + 47.35M subscription receipts (convert on close) + ~15.9M shares to the Covelya seller ($135M at $8.50). Pre-deal basic shares are ~306.5M.

net_income.notes: FY2024 net income flattered by an ~$8M deferred-tax recovery; FY2025 carried a $3.3M tax expense, hence the apparent drop despite higher EBITDA.

free_cash_flow.notes: FY2025 FCF deeply negative: operating CF $1.5M minus $30.3M growth capex (PP&E $26.5M + intangibles $3.8M) for the Nova Scotia battery facility and capacity build. Management guides FY2026 capex down to $15-18M, supporting FCF inflection.

growth_rates.growth_rate_rationale: Year-1 growth anchored to formal FY2026 guidance of $165-175M (midpoint $170M, +66% vs FY2025 $102.2M), which includes a partial-year contribution from the pending Covelya acquisition. Growth then decelerates from the mid-60s toward terminal as the business scales and the post-acquisition base normalizes.

assumptions.terminal_method: exit EV/EBITDA multiple (Gordon-growth floor retained); growth-stage profile makes a perpetuity-only terminal unrealistically low
assumptions.notes: WACC of 11% reflects TSXV/dual-use defense-tech small-cap risk, partly offset by a strong order book and 2026 guidance. Terminal value uses an exit EV/EBITDA multiple per scenario (Base 18x, Bull 26x, Bear 12x); a pure Gordon-growth terminal would understate value for a company still compounding 60%+. Net debt assumed ~$60M post-Covelya close (cash deployed into the $480M cash consideration, partly funded by $402.5M subscription receipts plus debt).

entry_price.calculation_notes: Entry price = Terminal Value per Share / (1.15)^5. Represents price to achieve a 15% CAGR over 5 years to the scenario terminal value. Even the bull-case entry of $4.11 sits below the current $6.24 price.

comparable_valuation.notes: At $6.24, EV/2026E-EBITDA is ~52x and EV/2026E-revenue ~14x. To justify the current price the base growth path requires a terminal EV/EBITDA of ~43x on year-5 EBITDA of ~$87M — i.e., the market assumes the stock still commands a hyper-growth multiple five years out. Defense-tech and marine-robotics peers trade in a 2-6x EV/revenue and low-double-digit EV/EBITDA range at maturity.

sanity_check.direction: overvaluation (market price above DCF, inverse of the SEK.NZ case)
trip_reasons: Market EV/2026E-EBITDA of ~52x is far above any defensible terminal multiple; even a generous 26x bull-case terminal multiple yields IV $5.21 (-17%).
Probability-weighted IV $2.96 is 53% below the current price; all three scenarios show negative upside.
Current price $6.24 sits in the upper half of the 10-year range (10yr low ~$0.13, recent high $8.50), indicating the market already prices in the growth and the Covelya deal.
sanity_check.diagnosis: This is a hyper-growth premium name: a standard FCF/EBITDA DCF cannot reproduce the market price without assuming the stock perpetually trades at a growth multiple. The valuation is driven by the terminal multiple assumption, to which IV is extremely sensitive.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Used scenario-specific exit EV/EBITDA terminal multiples (Base 18x, Bull 26x, Bear 12x) rather than Gordon-growth-only, which is the more defensible terminal method for a 60%+ grower; retained the Gordon-growth value as a documented floor. No artificial inflation of the base case to match price — the DCF is reported honestly as showing the stock is richly valued.

valuation_philosophy: PNG.V is valued by the market as a hyper-growth, dual-use subsea-defense compounder, not as a cash-flow-mature business. On a disciplined DCF anchored to FY2026 guidance ($170M revenue, $45M Adjusted EBITDA midpoint) and conservative-to-aggressive exit multiples (12-26x EV/EBITDA), intrinsic value spans roughly $1.08 (bear) to $5.21 (bull) with a base of $2.68 and a probability-weighted $2.96 — all below the current $6.24. To justify today's price the base path needs a ~43x terminal EV/EBITDA five years out. The investment case is therefore a momentum/optionality bet on (a) flawless execution of the $615M Covelya acquisition, (b) continued 30%+ organic growth, and (c) the market continuing to award a premium multiple. The fundamentals-based fair value supports accumulation only on a meaningful pullback (entry zone roughly $2-4); at $6.24 the DCF flags the stock as expensive.

investment_summary.recommendation: AVOID / HOLD on valuation - DCF intrinsic value well below market price
key_value_drivers: Covelya acquisition close and integration (expected end Q2 2026) - roughly doubles revenue
FY2026 guidance delivery ($165-175M revenue, $40-50M Adjusted EBITDA)
SeaPower battery and SAS order momentum and manufacturing scale-up
FCF inflection as growth capex normalizes from FY2025 peak ($30M to $15-18M)
Terminal multiple the market is willing to award a maturing defense-tech compounder
key_risks_to_valuation: Price embeds ~52x EV/2026E-EBITDA; multiple compression is the dominant downside risk
Covelya integration, regulatory approval, and post-deal leverage risk
Customer concentration (79% of Q1 2026 receivables from two customers)
Lumpy quarterly results and reliance on defense procurement timing
Dilution: subscription receipts, seller shares, and ongoing equity needs
investment_summary.thesis: Kraken is a high-quality, fast-growing marine-robotics and subsea-power franchise with genuine technology moats and strong order visibility, now pursuing a transformative $615M Covelya acquisition that should roughly double revenue. However, at $6.24 (CAD) the market already values it at ~52x 2026E EBITDA and ~14x revenue. A disciplined DCF puts fair value at roughly $2.68 base (range $1.08-$5.21), 53% below the current price on a probability-weighted basis. The thesis is a growth/momentum bet rather than a value opportunity; we would look to accumulate only on a material pullback toward the entry zone (~$2-4).
